rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card, impostor table and dated predictions before real data; synthetic validation at real offsets and masks (model-selection rates for four truths; two flawed newcomer estimators replaced before real data); 25 replication periods in two channels; three natives; exogenous re-activation refit; scorecard; frozen, guarded confirm script dry-run, not run.
rationale.faithfulness: Candia's biexponential is refuted as the village's decay law: it wins 5 of 27 fits, newcomers are not slower (powered), and the floor model wins most often. What holds is a clean descriptive law: fast decay (tau ~5 village days) to a small floor, among veterans who stay and with a closed roster. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F2 G0 H0 I1.
rationale.usefulness: A computable attention half-life for finished work (share 8% of its first-days value by days 21-40), a reason to re-inject old work explicitly rather than rely on memory, and a handover rule before retiring an agent (2 of 3 retirees' items died). Modest evidence; floor partly re-coinage.

one_line: Attention to a finished period falls with tau 5.5 village days to a 1.9% floor, carried alike by veterans and newcomers; Candia's biexponential wins 5/27 fits.
